capitals.name: Ain Farah
capitals.note: 'It was at one time the capital of the last Tunjur ruler, Shau Dorshid.' The page gives no coordinates, only 'about 130 kilometres northwest of El Fasher'; the dot is placed by that offset from El Fasher (13.63 N, 25.35 E), good to some tens of kilometres. The Sultanate of Darfur page has a version where Daali was a eunuch 'at the Tunjur capital of Uri'. No page names a Tunjur seat for 1551-1635 (Wadai: 'Tunjur heartland of Mondo' only for the late 17th century).

union.text: the Maba heartland around Wara and Abéché (the gazetteer's Wadai region inside Cliopatria's outline); the page gives no extent for the first century

correction.text: Darfur and Wadai under the Tunjur kings, with the capital at Ain Farah

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: all of Darfur plus the Wadai heartland, because the Tunjur 'became the ruling class of Darfur and Wadai' (Tunjur people page) and the Wadai page has 'the region ... ruled by the Tunjur kingdom' before the 1630s. No page gives an extent, a date for the founding beyond 'around the 15th century', or an infobox area (the Tunjur people page has no area), so the 561,000 km2 of the two regions is an upper bound, and the shape is soft.

correction.text: the Wadai heartland, the Tunjur kingdom's last land before 1635

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Darfur leaves after Daali's usurpation ('mid-16th century'), so only the Wadai heartland stays Tunjur until Abd al-Karim's rising of 1635. The Darfur page has Tunjur groups still in the south and east of Darfur when Sulayman Solong expanded (dated 1596-1637 or c. 1660-1680), which this shape ignores because the page gives no extent for them.

union.text: the Maba heartland around Wara and Abéché (the gazetteer's Wadai region inside Cliopatria's outline); the page gives no extent for the first century

region.text: Darfur and Wadai: the Tunjur 'ruling class of Darfur and Wadai'

ledger.note: Around the 15th century: the Tunjur kingdom exists in Darfur and Wadai. 'Prior to the 1630s, the region was ruled by the Tunjur kingdom, established around the 15th century' (Wadai page); the Tunjur people page has them as 'the ruling class of Darfur and Wadai in the 13th century' after 'peacefully taking power from the Daju', and the Darfur page has Ahmad al-Ma'qur as 'the founder of the Tunjur kingdom in Darfur' (undated). 1450 is the researcher's mid-century rounding of the Wadai page's century; the page gives no year or extent, so this is a bridge, not a date.

Mid-16th century: Daali takes the Jebel Marra from the last Tunjur king. 'The final Tunjur king was reportedly Shaw Dorshid', 'thought to have been around the mid-16th century'; Daali, his half-brother, was asked 'to usurp the kingship', and Shaw Dorshid 'fled to the Jebel Marra'. The infobox gives 'mid-16th century: Daali'; 1550 is sultanate-of-darfur's rounding.

Mid-16th century: the rest of Darfur passes out of Tunjur hands. The Darfur page does not say who held it between the Tunjur kingdom's fall and the Sultanate's wider outline of 1609 (sultanate-of-darfur ledger 1 gains it from nobody); the Tunjur are later found 'in the south and east' being brought under Sulayman's expansion, so the loss is a bridge, not a dated fact.

region.text: the Maba heartland around Wara and Abéché

ledger.note: 1635: Abd al-Karim overthrows the Tunjur king. 'overthrew the ruling Tunjur dynasty, who at the time was led by a king named "Daud"'; infobox 'Abd al-Karim overthrows the Tunjur King Daud'. The page names no boundary: the region is wadai-empire ledger 0's reading.

region.text: the Maba heartland around Wara and Abéché

ledger.note: 1635: the Tunjur kingdom ends in Wadai. The Tunjur people page has the Tunjur 'expelled from the Islamic Wadai empire by Abd-el-Kerim' 'around the middle of the 17th century' and later merged with the Fur; the Wadai page has them gone from the ruling position and, later, 'the Tunjur heartland of Mondo' reached by Wadai's expansion.

wars.name: Daali's usurpation of the Tunjur kingship
wars.outcome: Daali, half-brother of Shaw Dorshid, takes the kingship; Shaw Dorshid flees to the Jebel Marra (tradition).
wars.note: Not an article title: the Darfur page tells it as a story ('to ask his half-brother, Daali or Dalil Bahr, to usurp the kingship') and dates it 'mid-16th century'; the Tunjur people page has the Tunjur 'overthrown by an Arab' group in the 16th century.

wars.name: Abd al-Karim's rising against the Tunjur
wars.outcome: Abd al-Karim overthrows the Tunjur king Daud and founds the Wadai sultanate.
wars.note: Not an article title. 'In 1635, the Maba and other small groups in the region rallied to the Islamic banner of Abd al-Karim' (Wadai page); the page names no battle.

certainty.note: No page gives a Tunjur boundary, an area or a campaign map; the shapes are the gazetteer's Darfur and Wadai regions.

notes: No Cliopatria row exists for the Tunjur, so both keyframes are new. Four pages opened; none gives a Tunjur boundary, a date for the founding (the Wadai page says 'around the 15th century', the Tunjur people page says the 13th century for their rule in Darfur and Wadai), or an area. The start year 1450 is therefore a confidence-1 bridge. The kingdom is drawn as Darfur plus the Wadai heartland to the mid-16th century and the Wadai heartland alone to 1635, with the rest of Darfur passing to nobody, which is page-silent. Not settled: whether the Tunjur 'empire' of Darfur and the Tunjur of Wadai were one state or two (the Darfur page says Ahmad al-Ma'qur's son Musa 'went to Wadai and subjugated the region'; the Wadai page says Wadai was ruled by a Tunjur kingdom of its own); a gap-filler should open the Seshat or Cambridge History of Africa treatments. The Darfur page's 'Wadai paid tribute to Darfur as a legacy from the Tunjur empire' is not recorded as a vassal event because it is undated. The Daju (who held the region before, per the Tunjur people page) are a candidate dossier. No capital is recorded for 1551-1635.
